title: Study shows the 2008 recession caused people to identify with a lower class
titleZh: 为什么很多人会感觉自己混得更差
summary:
阶层认同是指个人在与他人比较时，对自身经济和社会地位的看法，这种认知会在很大程度上影响人们的幸福感、思维模式以及行为表现。既有研究表明，自我认同为较高社会阶层的人，通常身心健康水平更高，投票时更倾向于保守立场，且对社会发展预期更为乐观。不过，关于大规模经济变革如何影响人们的阶层认同，相关研究仍然十分有限。

来源：Phys.org；作者：Susan T. Mashiyama；原文发布时间：2025-12-23 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Class identity, which is how individuals view their economic and social positions in relation to others, has wide-ranging effects on people's well-being, thoughts, and behavior. Previous studies have shown that people who identify with a higher class have better physical and emotional health, tend to vote more conservatively, and have a more optimistic view of society. Yet there have been few studies examining how large-scale economic change affects class identity.
paragraphs.contentZh: 阶层认同是指个人在与他人比较时，对自身经济和社会地位的看法，这种认知会在很大程度上影响人们的幸福感、思维模式以及行为表现。既有研究表明，自我认同为较高社会阶层的人，通常身心健康水平更高，投票时更倾向于保守立场，且对社会发展预期更为乐观。不过，关于大规模经济变革如何影响人们的阶层认同，相关研究仍然十分有限。

paragraphs.contentEn: A new study published in Psychological Science led by Stephen Antonoplis, a UC Riverside assistant professor of psychology, showed that the 2008 recession, or Great Recession, caused people to identify with a lower class, and this was a long-lasting effect. Antonoplis' study contrasts with previous research in this area indicating that class identity is fairly stable over relatively long periods of time. Past analyses that did show shifts focused on short-term changes, especially those brought about by manipulations in the way the study subjects were asked to categorize themselves.
paragraphs.contentZh: 由加州大学河滨分校心理学助理教授斯蒂芬·安东诺普利斯牵头、发表于《心理科学》期刊的一项新研究指出，2008年的经济危机（即大衰退）使人们更倾向于认同自己属于较低社会阶层，且这一影响具有长期性。这一发现不同于此前该领域的研究所认为的“阶层认同在较长时间内相对稳定”。过去确实有研究观察到阶层认同的变化，但主要集中在短期波动，且通常是由于研究者在实验中操控受试者改变自我归类方式所致。

paragraphs.contentEn: Antonoplis said those studies typically used a "MacArthur ladder," a visual tool with 10 rungs representing different levels of resources such as money, education, and job quality. People on the top rung have the most resources, and those on the lowest rung have the least. One manipulation is to describe to different subject groups only the lowest or highest rung and ask them where they would place themselves. It turns out people tend to rate themselves a little higher when comparing themselves only to the lowest rung, and conversely, a little lower when thinking about only the highest.
paragraphs.contentZh: 安东诺普利斯指出，这类研究通常使用“麦克阿瑟阶梯”（MacArthur ladder），一种由10个阶梯组成的可视化测评工具，每一级代表不同的资源水平，如金钱、教育程度和工作质量。处在最上层阶梯的人拥有最多资源，而位于最下层的人资源最少。常见的一种实验操控是，仅向不同的受试群体描述阶梯的最低层或最高层，并让他们判断自己应处在什么位置。结果显示，当人们只与最低层进行比较时，往往会把自己评估得略高；反之，当只考虑最高层时，他们对自身位置的判断则会相对偏低。

paragraphs.contentEn: However, this effect is transient, said Antonoplis, and can change within just a few minutes. In contrast, his study focused on whether changes in class identity could last longer. His analyses, which utilized four large datasets that tracked the class identity of about 165,000 people over decades, showed that the changes he observed with the Great Recession were indeed long-term, lasting for years. Antonoplis stressed that the study only showed changes in class identity and did not examine how these corresponded to objective measures of losses in people's resources. He explained that class identity is a self-perception that is highly personal. "Invariably, there's someone in a study who reports an income of something like $200,000, yet identifies as lower class," he said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 但安东诺普利斯指出，这类由实验操控引发的效应通常只是暂时的，甚至可能在几分钟内就发生变化。相比之下，他的研究关注的是阶层认同的变化是否能够持续更长时间。他的分析基于四个大型数据集，这些数据集在数十年间追踪了约16.5万人的阶层认同变化，研究结果显示，大衰退期间出现的阶层认同变化确实具有长期性，其影响持续了多年。安东诺普利斯强调，该研究仅考察了阶层认同本身的变化，并没有分析这些变化是否与人们在资源方面的客观损失相对应。他解释说，阶层认同是一种高度个人化的自我感知。他举例说：“例如在研究中，总会有人报告年收入达到20万美元，却仍然将自己认同为低阶层。”

paragraphs.contentEn: In addition to the recession's material impacts, Antonoplis believes media messaging may have increased people's tendency to identify with lower classes. He observed that headlines during the era of the Great Recession were highly threatening and suggested that people's economic positions were falling precipitously and permanently. One example was, "When Greatness Slips Away"; and another was, "As Unemployment Rises, Kids' Future Dims." Such headlines were widespread across different news sources, including The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal.
paragraphs.contentZh: 安东诺普利斯认为，除了经济衰退带来的物质层面影响之外，媒体的信息传播也可能强化了人们认同较低阶层的倾向。他注意到，大衰退时期的新闻标题普遍渲染了强烈的危机感，暗示人们的经济地位正迅速且可能永久地下滑。例如，当时的标题有《当伟大悄然逝去》以及《随着失业率上升，孩子们的未来越发黯淡》。这类标题在多家新闻机构中广泛出现，包括《纽约时报》和《华尔街日报》。

paragraphs.contentEn: Antonoplis said the study identifies an additional pathway through which recessions might harm individuals. In addition to negative economic effects, the Great Recession has been linked to increases in adverse health outcomes for Americans. Perceived loss of status may be one reason for this. He said future research will explore how changes in people's class identity have impacted their health, as well as contributed to changes in the U.S. political landscape since the recession. These findings carry global implications since the U.S. Great Recession helped cause recessions in other countries.
paragraphs.contentZh: 安东诺普利斯表示，这项研究揭示了经济衰退损害个人福祉的另一条路径。除了直接的经济冲击之外，大衰退还被发现与美国人不良健康结果的增加有关。对社会地位下滑的主观感知，可能是其中一个原因。他指出，未来的研究将进一步探讨阶层认同的变化如何影响人们的健康状况，以及这种变化在大衰退之后如何推动了美国政治格局的转变。鉴于美国的大衰退曾波及其他国家并引发连锁衰退，这些发现也具有全球层面的意义。

paragraphs.contentEn: Antonoplis said increasing awareness of how historical events such as recessions affect people psychologically and impact their lives could help people be more resilient to them. "Most of the social implications of the study is probably about creating an accurate public memory," Antonoplis said. "It can be very confusing going through something like a big recession, and sometimes it's helpful to know that we've been through it before and what to expect."
paragraphs.contentZh: 安东诺普利斯认为，增进公众对经济衰退等历史事件如何从心理和现实生活两方面影响人们的认知，可能有助于提升人们面对此类冲击的韧性。他指出：“这项研究在社会层面的意义，或许主要在于建立一种准确的集体记忆。经历像大衰退这样的重大经济事件，本身就会让人感到困惑和不安，而知道我们曾共同渡过，并对未来有所准备，往往能帮助人们更好地应对。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Antonoplis added that the study might offer insight into the possible harm being caused by the "vibecession," which is a term that describes the feelings of insecurity many Americans are having right now about the nation's economy despite its strong overall performance. He thinks it is possible that issues related to inflation, cost-of-living, and media reporting on these changes could be leading to psychological and physical stress.
paragraphs.contentZh: 安东诺普利斯补充道，这项研究或许也能帮助人们理解当前所谓“氛围衰退”可能带来的危害，“氛围衰退”指的是尽管整体经济数据强劲，但许多美国民众仍对国家经济抱有不安全感。他认为，通货膨胀、生活成本的上升，以及媒体对这些变化的报道，都可能是造成人们身心压力的原因。
